frame: game metres, x east, z south, y absolute (Arc de Triumf ground = 0)
channel_howto: For each channel point: water surface = line y; bank top = bank_y (≈DEM, street level). Carve terrain at lateral distance d from the line: y = min(groundY, water - bed_below_water) for d <= top_w/2, else min(groundY, water + (d - top_w/2)/slope). Water mesh level = line y (slopes downstream ~0.6 m/km), not the lake-style single level. Bridges over it keep their decks at street level.

earthworks.evidence: Street View Constantin P. Apr 2025 on Albișoara (47.04090,28.83405 hdg 30): water not visible from the road; far slab slope spans ~3.5°→12.4° below horizon at ~34→23 m → water ≈3.0 m below bank top. Esri img/mv_canal_crop.png: lit slab slope ≈5.7 m wide in plan (→ ~1:2), dark water+shade ≈15.7 m → water ≈10 m wide, top width ≈22 m. Ion Bragari pano (47.03882,28.83866 hdg 40): banks on both sides at street level. Game water polygons here are only 3-11 m wide and sit ~0.3 m below the DEM (= road level). 2020 AGCC ortho cross-sections at s≈2950/3150/3300 (Podul Circului ±150 m): rim to rim 20-22 m, slab slope ~8 m in plan on the NE side, water+shade ~9 m, SW slope ~4-5 m of shrubs down to Albișoara's kerb; old 10 m bed + 1:2 slopes (~26 m) ran 3 m into Albișoara. Ground photos (Podul Circului, trolleybus aerial) show no railings along the canal. Line moved 2 m NE for ±130 m around Podul Circului to the ortho rim-to-rim centre (it ran Albișoara's kerb into the SW slope).
